title: Fourteen Miles and One Bend
subtitle: 几何图形 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 几何图形（科学与技术·数学与图形）
meta: 主题语境：几何图形（科学与技术·数学与图形）　|　核心词汇：curve　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 curve 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1949 the surveyor ① drew a curve that no engineer in the district would have approved, and he said the drawing was the whole of the survey. The ② curve, meaning the line and not the bend in the road, ran fourteen miles and stayed unpainted on the plan; a curve, he said, is the only thing on a drawing that is judged by how long it is left unmeasured.

Every ③ curve in that plan had the same radius against it, and the ④ curve at the end, meaning the one he kept for the river bend and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever checked twice. A curve, his assistant said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to measure; the surveyor said the measuring is the part that fills fourteen miles.

The road builder meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the curve was the whole of the road, meaning the bend and not the line. The ⑥ curve, meaning the bend and not any of that, is the only thing on a road that everybody slows for and nobody straightens; curve, he said, is either something you draw or the only word that means both a line and a bend. He said the bend is the part they remember.

By 1957 the ⑦ curve had become a line in a specification, and the specification had become an argument about the radius. The ⑧ curve of the whole thing, the surveyor wrote in July, was one plan and fourteen miles of measuring; curve, he said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to measure. She said the measuring was never mentioned.

The ⑨ curve I remember is the one at the end, which was resurveyed in 1966 and is still described as the sharpest in the district. A ⑩ curve, the assistant said in 1968, is the only thing that improves by being measured; every curve, she said, is a bend that has agreed to look like a line. She said the bend was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 曲线（指图纸上画出的那一条）
B. n. 曲线（指那条线本身，与路上那个弯相对）
C. 固定搭配：draw a curve 画一条曲线
D. n. 曲线（指留给河道转弯处的那一条）
E. n. 曲线；曲度（抽象总称，指一整张图纸的弧度）
F. n. 曲线（指技术说明里写到、被规定的那一条）
G. n. 弯道；转弯处（指路上车辆减速通过的那一段）
H. n. 弯道（抽象总称，指被拉直不了的那个弯）

answers.why: draw a curve 意为“画一条曲线”，1949 年测量员画了一条全地区没有一位工程师会批准的曲线。
curve 意为“曲线”，指那条线本身而不是路上那个弯，它在图纸上延续了十四英里而从未被描实。
curve 意为“曲线”，指那张图纸上每一条曲线，每一条都有同一个半径对着它。
curve 意为“曲线”，指留给河道转弯处的那一条，是唯一有人复核过两次的。
curve 意为“弯道、转弯处”，指路上车辆减速通过的那一段，筑路人说这个弯就是那条路的全部。
curve 意为“弯道”，指被拉直不了的那个弯而不是别的，是路上人人都减速、却无人去取直的东西。
curve 意为“曲线”，指技术说明里写到、被规定的那一条，到 1957 年这条曲线成了说明里的一行。
curve 意为“曲线、曲度”，测量员七月写道，整件事的曲度是一张图纸和十四英里的丈量。
curve 意为“弯道”，我记得的是末尾那一个，1966 年被重测，至今仍被说成全地区最急的。
curve 为抽象总称，助手 1968 年说，一条曲线是唯一会因为被丈量而变得更好的东西。
